summary: Generalizes the 'own-enters-play' Reaction window (issue #152), previously opened only by Purchase(), to every entry point: Equip (Items/Followers), PlayStrategy's Terrain path, and equip-battle's Spell attach -- addressing the 'no Equip-time entry hook' gap flagged in Follower Wave 2's triage (issue #148), the highest-leverage remaining primitive by card count. New shared EntryReactionAbility/OpenEntryReactionWindow helpers. Repeatable per entry (clears any earlier AbilityUses record when opening), and PendingChoice.ActingPlayerId now controls post-close priority (defaults preserve existing Purchase/attackReaction behavior; Equip/Terrain/equip-battle correctly cede to the opponent). Exercising a Terrain's own ability for the first time surfaced and fixed two latent bugs: ValidateAbility's zone check assumed every Strategy source is in Hand (a Terrain stays in Zone.Battlefield), and UseAbility's tail would have wrongly auto-discarded a Terrain using its own ability. Shared-file note: all changed files are within L5R.Core (rules engine) and its test suite, plus docs/ROADMAP.md -- a single rules-lane primitive change; no UI/client files touched.
validation: New GeneralizedEntryReactionWindow test (3 scenarios: Equip opens+resolves+correctly cedes priority to the opponent; a stale earlier-entry usage record does not block a fresh window; PlayStrategy's Terrain path opens+resolves+cedes priority). Full suite: 95/95 core + 34/34 published + 8/8 deck format pass. bash tools/check.sh --skip-client passes.
remaining: No mechanism yet returns a card to play from a discard pile or the Fate deck, so that entry path (explicitly named in the user's spec) is not exercised by any real card yet; the hook needs no further change to support it once such a mechanism is built.
